name: Nissan 300ZX (Z32)
h1: Nissan 300ZX Twin Turbo (Z32, 1990–1996): specs, VG30DETT engine and what owners say

nhtsa.note: NHTSA files every 300ZX under 300ZX, turbo and non-turbo alike, so these counts include the non-turbo cars. They are the Z32 model years 1990–1996 only.

us.x: Sold new in the US for model years 1990 to 1996, as the non-turbo 300ZX and the 300ZX Twin Turbo. The last 300 US cars included a Commemorative Edition. In Japan it was sold as the Fairlady Z until 2000.

fame.x: Motor Trend named the 300ZX its 1990 Import Car of the Year.
Car and Driver put the Z32 on its Ten Best list for seven years in a row, every model year it was sold in the US.

A Cunningham-prepared 300ZX won the 1994 24 Hours of Daytona and the 12 Hours of Sebring. At Le Mans that year, Steve Millen, Johnny O’Connell and John Morton won the IMSA GTS class and finished fifth overall. Millen and Nissan took the 1994 IMSA GTS drivers’ and manufacturers’ titles.
Nissan used a Cray-2 supercomputer to design the Z32, which Wikipedia calls one of the first production cars designed with CAD software.

fame.t: The Super Bowl ad that aired once
fame.x: Ridley Scott directed a 300ZX Twin Turbo ad for the 1990 Super Bowl. It aired only once before Nissan pulled it, reportedly over fears it promoted street racing.

gens.tag: 3.0-liter twin-turbo VG30DETT V6, 300 hp (US manual), 5-speed manual or 4-speed automatic, rear-drive. Non-turbo: 222 hp.

variants.name: 300ZX Twin Turbo

hp.note: at 6,400 rpm with the 5-speed manual; 280 hp with the automatic

variants.what: Twin turbos with twin intercoolers, Super HICAS four-wheel steering, an adjustable two-mode suspension and thicker brake discs than the non-turbo car.

variants.name: 300ZX (non-turbo)

top.note: Car and Driver’s 1989 test; Hagerty UK says 149 mph

trans.note: Hagerty UK says the automatic slowed 0-60 to 7.5 seconds

variants.what: The non-turbo car, with the same body. It came as a two-seater and a 2+2, and a convertible joined the range in 1993.

variants.name: Fairlady Z Twin Turbo (Japan)

hp.note: 280 PS (206 kW) at 6,400 rpm, Nissan’s figure under Japan’s gentlemen’s agreement (JDM)

tq.note: lb-ft at 3,600 rpm, converted from Nissan’s 388 Nm (JDM)

variants.what: The Japanese car, badged Fairlady Z and rated at 280 PS. Hagerty UK says the turbo really made about 300 bhp wherever it was sold.

VG30DETT.name: Nissan VG30DETT
facts: V6, DOHC 24-valve, iron block, aluminum heads, belt-driven cams
300 hp at 6,400 rpm and 283 lb-ft at 3,600 rpm (US manual); 280 hp with the automatic; 280 PS in Japan
Two Garrett/Mitsubishi T22/TB02 hybrid turbos in parallel, made just for Nissan, with two intercoolers

issues.t: Turbo failure, and the engine comes out to fix it
issues.x: SlashGear, citing Car and Driver, says the turbo seals can start leaking between 60,000 and 80,000 miles. Writing on Jalopnik about his own car, Peter Monshizadeh found a seized turbo and says the engine bay is so cramped that the easiest way to replace the turbos is to pull the engine.

Jalopnik’s owner found two dead fuel injectors during his rebuild, and another failed about 3,000 miles later. He says the old-style injectors don’t like ethanol fuel. SlashGear, citing Autocar, says injectors can stick and cause misfires, and Hagerty UK says to listen for a ticking from the coils or injectors.

Hagerty UK says a new timing belt is needed every 60,000 miles, and to judge it on age as well as mileage. Jalopnik gives 60,000 miles or four years, whichever comes first. Hagerty UK also says to check for oil leaks at the cam end seals.
issues.fix: Replace the timing belt every 60,000 miles or four years.

issues.x: Hagerty UK says this engine runs hot as standard, so the cooling system must be perfect, and that the heat can damage the wiring loom. Jalopnik’s owner found the rubber brake-booster vacuum hoses old and cracked, and says the many plenum vacuum hoses are hard to refit.

VG30DE.name: Nissan VG30DE
facts: V6, DOHC 24-valve, with N-VCT variable valve timing
222 hp at 6,400 rpm, 198 lb-ft at 4,800 rpm in the Z32

issues.x: Hagerty UK says the 300ZX needs a new timing belt every 60,000 miles, and to judge it on age as well as mileage.
issues.fix: Replace the timing belt every 60,000 miles.
